name: NetAlertX (network presence scanner)
param_style: python sqlite3; mostly f-string SQL with helper fragments and constants inlined, ? positional where user input is bound
schema_source: server/db/schema/app.sql plus DB.initDB() steps in server/database.py and server/db/db_upgrade.py (ensure_column, ensure_Indexes, ensure_views, triggers) and server/db/db_history.py (audit triggers); only the CREATE statements the queries need, fetched not vendored (GPL)
data_scale: scale 1: 400 devices (140 mobile with ~300 sessions each over 90 days, stationary/IoT/infra/servers with NIC children; 7 archived, 11 new), ~93k Events and ~46k Sessions, one in-flight CurrentScan of ~530 rows, 75k Plugins_History rows over 6 plugins, ~750 Plugins_Objects, 6000 AppEvents, 2000 Online_History, 43k Resource_History rows, ~300 Settings; about 90 MB. #769's reporter had a 1.7 GB database
visibility_note: 7.3k stars (formerly Pi.Alert); a popular Docker / Home Assistant add-on network presence monitor; SQLite is its only database
interest_note: A 5-minute scan loop that recomputes everything from scratch: DevicesView (50 IFNULLs + per-device correlated EXISTS ... GROUP BY HAVING over Events) scanned many times per cycle, LatestEventsPerMAC windowing the whole Events table, Sessions rebuilt from a self-joined UNION view, nested NOT EXISTS presence predicates, 41-statement audit triggers on every Devices update, and full-table JSON exports.
reach_note: widely self-hosted (Docker, Unraid, Home Assistant add-on); SQLite is the only backend

cpu_evidence.summary: constant high CPU and memory with a 1.7 GB database; DBCLNP cleanup timed out at 30 s, ~15 s on the Plugins_History trim and then killed at the Plugins_Objects dedupe
high CPU while idle; the per-loop JSON exports (sql_devices_all, sql_events_all, sql_events_pending_alert, sql_appevents, sql_settings) named as suspects
follow-up to #769: DB grows back to 300 MB within hours, DBCLNP timeouts, PHP exhausting 128 MB reading the exported query JSON, 'database is locked'
9k devices: Devices page takes 12+ s, filtering takes minutes, Network page never loads
6k+ devices: opening one device shows a loading spinner for ~10 s with a CPU spike
steady 6-12 % CPU of 2 cores with only ARP and MQTT enabled; per-cycle work in the main loop
